dissenting_views: Meta-optimisation offers the best Sharpe (0.43 ex-ante, 0.68 backtest), needs no repair, and has the smallest drawdown (-23.2%). I declined it because 37% rests on max_sharpe, which breaches the drawdown limit on its own, got zero vote points, and was criticised for amplifying one CMA spread into a 51% value-equity position.

resampled_efficient_frontier won the vote (49 points, composite 1.000) and would need no repair as a single method. I declined it because its -24.8% drawdown is 16bp from the limit, which the CRO and two reviewers call fragile, and its 4.51% tracking error is the highest of the offered options.

The regime confidence of 0.35 argues against any regime-conditioned blend, and the paper's own late-cycle choice was inverse tracking-error weighting. I kept regime_conditional because its statistics are essentially those of the unconditional blends, and because its repair (6.1% of the portfolio) is smaller than inverse tracking-error's (7.2%) and its breadth larger (12.4 against 9.8 effective candidates).

Three shortlisted ingredients (cvar_minimization, black_litterman, risk_parity) share the CRO's binding risk: a joint stock-bond sell-off of the 2022 or 1970s kind. The blend does not diversify this away, and the repaired drawdown leaves only about 1.7 points of headroom.

inverse_volatility gained weight in the repair, but reviewers found its diversification overstated: an implicit 43% credit and sovereign spread cluster, plus a minor technical error equating inverse volatility with equal risk contribution.
black_litterman is the largest single share (11%). A reviewer found its equilibrium prior double-counts overlapping US equity ETFs, which may distort its large-cap and value split.

market_cap_weight was bottom-flagged on 14 of 15 ballots, with a -40.6% drawdown. It is one of the ensemble's inputs, but its composite of 0.000 means it carries little weight. I note the dissent and do not rely on it.
invalidation_conditions: Re-estimated ex-ante volatility of the held portfolio falls below 8.0% or rises above 12.0% at a quarterly rebalance. Either is an IPS hard breach requiring re-optimisation.
The portfolio's realised peak-to-trough drawdown reaches -20%. This is an early-warning trigger set 5 points inside the -25% IPS limit, given the backtest's -23.3% leaves little headroom.

The rolling 12-month correlation between US large-cap equity and intermediate Treasury returns turns positive and stays above +0.3 for a full quarter. That breaks the stock-bond hedge the main ingredients rely on.
The macro agent moves its regime call away from expansion (to late-cycle, contraction or stagflation), or its confidence remains below 0.4 at the next quarterly review.
The equity CMA for US large-cap or US value is cut by 1 percentage point or more, or the intermediate-Treasury CMA moves by 75bp or more. Either changes the blend's return and risk balance.
Ex-ante tracking error to the 60/30/10 benchmark rises above 5.0%, leaving less than 1 point of the 6% budget.
High-yield credit spreads widen by 200bp or more within a quarter. That would activate the credit and sovereign cluster carried in via inverse_volatility and risk_parity.
body.rationale:
I recommend the regime-conditional ensemble. It needed the smallest repair of any averaging ensemble, it spreads weight most widely across methods, and it has the highest composite score (0.799). It does this without leaning on any single candidate.

The trade I am making: I give up about 0.04 of ex-ante Sharpe (0.39 against 0.43) and 0.05 of backtest Sharpe (0.63 against 0.68) relative to the meta-optimisation. In return I get breadth across 13 candidates (12.4 effective) instead of 4 (3.8 effective). The meta-optimisation rests 37% on max_sharpe. That candidate breaches the -25% drawdown limit on its own (-25.9%), received zero vote points, and reviewers said its 51% value-equity bet amplifies a single CMA difference. Concentrating on it would import exactly the estimation risk the review process flagged.

I also rejected the single-method option, the resampled efficient frontier. It was the top vote-winner, but its -24.8% drawdown sits 16bp inside the limit, which both reviewers and the CRO call fragile.

Among the averaging ensembles the outcomes are nearly indistinguishable: all are at 8.00% volatility, 3.7-4.1% tracking error and about -23.3% to -23.4% drawdown. So the size and direction of the repair is the deciding factor.

The repair is a real cost and I own it. Unrepaired, the blend had 7.52% volatility, below the 8% floor. To fix this, 13.6% of the ensemble weight was moved between candidates, which changed 6.1% of the portfolio:
- cvar_minimization gained 3pp and inverse_volatility gained 3pp. Both are top-three in the vote and IPS-compliant on both checks.
- pc_researcher lost 7pp. It breaches the return, volatility and tracking-error limits, and two reviewers found an unreconciled Sharpe figure.
- hierarchical_risk_parity lost 3pp. It breaches volatility and tracking error.

I would defend that shift: weight moved from non-compliant, low-voted methods to compliant, peer-approved ones. The price is that drawdown headroom narrowed from -21.7% to -23.3%, leaving about 1.7 points inside the limit. The volatility also sits exactly at the 8% floor, so compliance on volatility is engineered rather than comfortable.

On the regime: the macro agent's confidence is only 0.35, which is below the IPS threshold of 0.4. I am therefore not choosing this ensemble for its regime tilt. Its statistics are nearly identical to the backtest-Sharpe-weighted and simple-average blends, which tells me the expansion call is not driving the allocation much. That is the property I want when the regime call is weak.

Key assumptions:
- Treasuries continue to offset equity stress. The CRO named this the binding risk for cvar_minimization, black_litterman and risk_parity, which together carry meaningful weight here.
- The judged CMAs are not materially biased.
- The 1993-onward covariance panel is a fair guide to the next three years.

Inherited weaknesses:
- black_litterman is the largest single share at 11%. A reviewer found its equilibrium prior double-counts overlapping equity ETFs.
- inverse_volatility carries a hidden credit and sovereign spread cluster of about 43% of its own weight.
- risk_parity entered as revised with an ex-ante volatility of 7.84% and a drawdown not re-checked. The blend, not the component, is what is held to the IPS.

board_memo.recommendation:
We recommend a blended portfolio that combines the allocations proposed by 13 of the 15 investment methods we evaluated, using the 'regime-conditional' blending rule. No single method's view dominates: the largest contribution from any one method is about 11%.

The blend had to be adjusted slightly to meet the policy's minimum risk level. Weight was moved toward the methods the review panel rated most highly, and away from methods that broke policy limits on their own. This changed about 6% of the portfolio.
board_memo.macro_rationale: The macro team's best reading is that the economy is in expansion, but it holds that view with low confidence (0.35 on a 0-1 scale). We therefore chose a blend whose results barely depend on the regime call: it looks almost identical to the plain averages of the methods. In other words, we did not bet heavily on the expansion view. Instead, we spread the portfolio across many approaches so that no single forecast drives the outcome.
board_memo.largest_positions: Intermediate-term US Treasuries are the largest holding at about 15%, followed by US large-cap stocks at about 14% and long-term US Treasuries at about 9%. The rest is spread across US value, growth and small-cap stocks, international stocks, corporate and international bonds, gold and other real assets. In total the portfolio holds the equivalent of about 15 equally-sized positions.
board_memo.changes_since_last_review:
No prior recommended allocation was supplied to this review, so this is the first recommendation recorded under the ratified IPS v0.2. Within this review, two adjustments were made to the raw blend:
- To lift its risk from 7.5% to the 8% policy floor, weight moved toward the CVaR-minimisation and inverse-volatility methods (about +3 points each).
- Weight moved away from the maximum-entropy method (-7 points) and the hierarchical risk parity method (-3 points). Both broke policy limits on their own.
key_risks: Stocks and bonds falling together, as in 2022 or the 1970s. Much of the portfolio's protection assumes Treasuries rise when stocks fall, so this would hit the largest holdings at once.
Limited room under the loss limit. The historical worst loss of -23.3% is only about 1.7 points from the -25% policy limit.
Risk at the policy floor. Volatility sits exactly at the 8% minimum, so small changes in markets or estimates could push it outside the band at a rebalance.
Credit stress. A meaningful share of the portfolio is in corporate, high-yield, international and emerging-market bonds, which tend to fall together when credit spreads widen.
Uncertain economic regime. The macro team's confidence in its expansion call is low, so return forecasts carry extra uncertainty.
Lagging the benchmark in a strong US equity rally, because the portfolio holds less US large-cap stock than the benchmark.

escalations: regime_confidence_below: the macro agent's regime confidence is 0.35, below 0.4; action: flag_in_board_memo. Macro agent's regime confidence is low; downstream CMAs inherit that uncertainty.
